AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.label: International AI rules and governance
AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.definition: Calls for, or discussion of, international rules, norms, legal frameworks, standards, treaties or cooperative mechanisms to govern AI, including arguments that governance must keep pace with AI and must balance innovation with protection.
AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.inclusion: Passages urging common/binding/global rules, regulation, guardrails, norms, principles or multilateral cooperation on AI; references to non-UN governance initiatives (G7 Hiroshima Process, G20, AI safety summits, GPAI) as governance.
AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.exclusion: Purely national regulation (AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY); UN-specific bodies and processes (AI_UN_ROLE); demands centred on developing countries' voice in rule-making (AI_INCLUSIVE_GOVERNANCE); rejection of international governance (AI_GOVERNANCE_SKEPTICISM); weapons-specific rules (AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS).
AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.boundary_cases: A passage calling for global rules through the UN can take both AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE and AI_UN_ROLE. Generic 'responsible AI' wording without any governance mechanism or call for rules is coded here only if it addresses how AI should be governed collectively.

AI_INCLUSIVE_GOVERNANCE.label: Equal voice in AI rule-making
AI_INCLUSIVE_GOVERNANCE.definition: Demands that developing, African, small or all states have a meaningful, equal say in setting AI rules and standards, and objections to AI rules being written by a few states or in exclusive formats outside the UN.
AI_INCLUSIVE_GOVERNANCE.inclusion: Passages insisting that the Global South, Africa, small states or every country participate in shaping AI governance; criticism that AI rules are made by narrow clubs or favour some nations.
AI_INCLUSIVE_GOVERNANCE.exclusion: Unequal access to AI technology or benefits without a rule-making claim (AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE); general calls for 'inclusive' governance with no claim about who sets the rules (AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE).
AI_INCLUSIVE_GOVERNANCE.boundary_cases: When a passage links mineral supply or market size to a demand for a seat at the AI rule-making table, code here (and AI_RESOURCE_FOOTPRINT only if resource demand is discussed).

AI_GOVERNANCE_SKEPTICISM.label: Scepticism of AI regulation and risk narratives
AI_GOVERNANCE_SKEPTICISM.definition: Rejection of or scepticism toward international AI governance, preemptive regulation, AI pauses, catastrophic-risk warnings or the UN's role on AI, typically favouring national control, acceleration or light-touch rules.
AI_GOVERNANCE_SKEPTICISM.inclusion: Passages rejecting 'globalist' or international control of AI, arguing against moratoria or preemptive regulation, dismissing AI doom warnings as alarmism, or framing AI anxiety as paranoia.
AI_GOVERNANCE_SKEPTICISM.exclusion: Calls to balance innovation and regulation that still endorse governance (AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE); criticism that the UN is sidelined or too slow while asking it to do more (AI_UN_ROLE).
AI_GOVERNANCE_SKEPTICISM.boundary_cases: A speaker who acknowledges some risks but rejects international oversight is coded here; acknowledging risks alone is not scepticism.

AI_UN_ROLE.label: UN bodies and processes on AI
AI_UN_ROLE.definition: References to the UN system's role on AI: the Secretary-General's advisory body, Tech Envoy, Global Digital Compact, Pact for the Future, Independent International Scientific Panel on AI, Global Dialogue on AI Governance, GA/Security Council agenda items, UNESCO initiatives, or the UN using AI for its own work.
AI_UN_ROLE.inclusion: Passages supporting, criticising, leading or proposing UN AI bodies, resolutions, processes or agenda items; the UN as the central forum for AI decisions; AI to make the UN more efficient.
AI_UN_ROLE.exclusion: International governance calls that do not mention the UN system or its instruments (AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE).
AI_UN_ROLE.boundary_cases: Criticism that the UN lags or is bypassed counts here when it calls for a UN role; outright rejection of a UN role is AI_GOVERNANCE_SKEPTICISM.

AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS.label: Military AI and autonomous weapons
AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS.definition: AI in warfare, weapons and strategic security: lethal autonomous weapons systems, military targeting, AI in nuclear command and escalation, and calls for rules, bans or human control over military AI.
AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS.inclusion: Passages on autonomous weapons, machines deciding life and death, AI on the battlefield, military AI norms or treaties, AI as a strategic/arms-control risk alongside nuclear, cyber and space.
AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS.exclusion: Non-military AI safety or loss-of-control risks (AI_SAFETY_EXISTENTIAL); criminal or terrorist misuse and cyberattacks (AI_CYBER_SECURITY); AI used to support arms-control verification or peace (AI_PEACE_APPLICATIONS).
AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS.boundary_cases: Human control of weapons is coded here, not AI_HUMAN_CONTROL. A list of threats merely naming 'AI' next to war is AI_THREAT_LIST_MENTION unless military use of AI is stated.

AI_PEACE_APPLICATIONS.label: AI as a tool for peace
AI_PEACE_APPLICATIONS.definition: AI presented as a tool for diplomacy, mediation, conflict prevention, arms-control verification or as a force that should serve peace rather than domination.
AI_PEACE_APPLICATIONS.inclusion: Passages proposing AI for early warning of conflict, mediation, translation for diplomacy, treaty verification, or insisting AI serve peace not domination.
AI_PEACE_APPLICATIONS.exclusion: AI for development, health or climate (AI_DEVELOPMENT_SDGS); military AI risks (AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS).
AI_PEACE_APPLICATIONS.boundary_cases: Disaster early warning is development/climate (AI_DEVELOPMENT_SDGS), not peace, unless conflict prevention is stated.

AI_SAFETY_EXISTENTIAL.label: Frontier AI safety and loss of control
AI_SAFETY_EXISTENTIAL.definition: Technical and catastrophic AI risks: frontier model safety, misalignment, superintelligence, loss of control, uncontrolled or ungoverned AI as a survival or existential threat, and safety testing before release.
AI_SAFETY_EXISTENTIAL.inclusion: Passages warning of AI escaping human control, existential or species-level risk, superintelligence, safety requirements for the most capable models.
AI_SAFETY_EXISTENTIAL.exclusion: Military uses (AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS); general normative insistence that humans stay in charge without a safety-risk claim (AI_HUMAN_CONTROL); disinformation or crime (their own codes).
AI_SAFETY_EXISTENTIAL.boundary_cases: A brief 'uncontrolled use of AI' warning with no catastrophic or technical safety content goes to AI_OPPORTUNITY_RISK_DUALITY or AI_THREAT_LIST_MENTION.

AI_HUMAN_CONTROL.label: Human agency, control and accountability
AI_HUMAN_CONTROL.definition: Normative insistence that humans remain in control of AI and responsible for AI-assisted decisions, that people stay subjects rather than objects of algorithms, and that human judgment, autonomy and legal accountability be preserved.
AI_HUMAN_CONTROL.inclusion: Passages saying technology must remain under human control, humans must be masters of AI, decisions must stay with accountable people, or warning against outsourcing human thought and free will to machines.
AI_HUMAN_CONTROL.exclusion: Human control of weapons (AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS); catastrophic loss-of-control risk (AI_SAFETY_EXISTENTIAL); broad human rights and ethics language without the control/agency claim (AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS).
AI_HUMAN_CONTROL.boundary_cases: 'Human-centred AI' alone is AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS; it is coded here only when human control, decision authority or accountability is explicit.

AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS.label: Human rights, ethics and democracy
AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS.definition: AI framed through human rights, dignity, ethics, privacy, surveillance, human-centred design and democratic values, including risks of repression, algorithmic control of citizens and erosion of democratic accountability.
AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS.inclusion: Passages calling for human-centred, rights-based or ethical AI, protection of privacy and freedoms, warning of AI surveillance or repression, or tying AI to democracy and accountability.
AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS.exclusion: Discrimination, stereotypes and cultural/linguistic exclusion (AI_BIAS_CULTURAL_DIVERSITY); children specifically (AI_CHILD_PROTECTION); disinformation (AI_DISINFORMATION).
AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS.boundary_cases: Ethics invoked as part of a call for international rules takes both this code and AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

AI_BIAS_CULTURAL_DIVERSITY.label: Bias, stereotypes and cultural diversity
AI_BIAS_CULTURAL_DIVERSITY.definition: AI reproducing bias, prejudice, hate or stereotypes, distorting or censoring history, misrepresenting peoples, and threatening or protecting linguistic and cultural diversity.
AI_BIAS_CULTURAL_DIVERSITY.inclusion: Passages on biased training data, discrimination, AI spreading hatred or stereotypes, digital erasure of non-hegemonic cultures, fair representation in AI-mediated knowledge, preserving small languages or multilingualism.
AI_BIAS_CULTURAL_DIVERSITY.exclusion: General human rights or ethics language without bias or cultural content (AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS); disinformation campaigns (AI_DISINFORMATION).
AI_BIAS_CULTURAL_DIVERSITY.boundary_cases: AI used to protect small languages (a positive application) is coded here because the concern is cultural diversity.

AI_DISINFORMATION.label: Disinformation and information integrity
AI_DISINFORMATION.definition: AI-enabled misinformation, disinformation, deepfakes, manipulation of public opinion, election interference and threats to information integrity.
AI_DISINFORMATION.inclusion: Passages linking AI to fake content, deepfakes, propaganda, manipulated elections or the erosion of shared facts.
AI_DISINFORMATION.exclusion: Hate speech and stereotypes without a falsehood claim (AI_BIAS_CULTURAL_DIVERSITY); cybercrime (AI_CYBER_SECURITY).
AI_DISINFORMATION.boundary_cases: A list naming 'artificial intelligence' and 'disinformation' as separate items does not link them; code AI_THREAT_LIST_MENTION unless the text connects AI to disinformation.

AI_CYBER_SECURITY.label: Cyber threats, crime and terrorist misuse
AI_CYBER_SECURITY.definition: AI misuse by criminals, terrorists or hostile actors: cyberattacks, cybercrime, attacks on critical infrastructure, online crime, and AI within international information-security frameworks.
AI_CYBER_SECURITY.inclusion: Passages on AI-enabled cyberattacks, fraud, trafficking, terrorism or hybrid threats, and on cybercrime cooperation covering AI.
AI_CYBER_SECURITY.exclusion: State military use of AI in warfare (AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS); disinformation (AI_DISINFORMATION).
AI_CYBER_SECURITY.boundary_cases: Passages that discuss only cyberspace or new technologies without naming AI are not AI evidence.

AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.label: AI divide and equitable access
AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.definition: Inequality in access to AI and its benefits between and within countries: risks of a new AI divide, North-South gaps, developing countries as passive consumers, and calls to share AI benefits with all.
AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.inclusion: Passages warning AI will widen gaps or leave countries behind, demanding equitable access or benefit-sharing, or envisioning AI for all.
AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.exclusion: Concrete support measures such as training, funding or technology transfer (AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING); rule-making voice (AI_INCLUSIVE_GOVERNANCE); concentration of power in firms or states (AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION).
AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.boundary_cases: When a passage states both the divide and a remedy (e.g. capacity building), apply both codes.

AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING.label: Capacity building and AI cooperation
AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING.definition: Concrete cooperation to build AI capabilities: skills, training, technology transfer, financing, infrastructure, regional AI centres and bilateral or South-South AI partnerships.
AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING.inclusion: Passages offering or requesting AI training, funds, compute, infrastructure, knowledge sharing, regional centres or partnerships.
AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING.exclusion: Statements of inequality without a support measure (AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE); a country's own domestic programmes (AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY).
AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING.boundary_cases: A country offering its national AI experience to others takes this code and AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY.

AI_DEVELOPMENT_SDGS.label: AI for development and the SDGs
AI_DEVELOPMENT_SDGS.definition: AI as a means to advance sustainable development, growth, health, agriculture, education systems, public services, climate action and disaster early warning, including particular value for small and island states.
AI_DEVELOPMENT_SDGS.inclusion: Passages presenting AI as a tool for the SDGs, poverty reduction, health, food security, climate mitigation or adaptation, disaster prediction or better services.
AI_DEVELOPMENT_SDGS.exclusion: Jobs and labour-market effects (AI_ECONOMY_LABOR); environmental costs of AI (AI_RESOURCE_FOOTPRINT); a country describing its own AI investments (AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY).
AI_DEVELOPMENT_SDGS.boundary_cases: If AI is only listed among technologies that could help development without elaboration, prefer AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION.

AI_RESOURCE_FOOTPRINT.label: Energy, minerals and environmental footprint
AI_RESOURCE_FOOTPRINT.definition: Material demands of AI: energy and water consumption, data-centre footprints, and rising demand for critical minerals, including producer countries' claims about value addition.
AI_RESOURCE_FOOTPRINT.inclusion: Passages linking AI to energy demand, water or land use, emissions of AI infrastructure, or critical-mineral supply.
AI_RESOURCE_FOOTPRINT.exclusion: AI used to fight climate change (AI_DEVELOPMENT_SDGS); chip supply-chain rivalry (AI_GEOPOLITICAL_RIVALRY).
AI_RESOURCE_FOOTPRINT.boundary_cases: Minerals raised mainly to claim a rule-making seat also take AI_INCLUSIVE_GOVERNANCE.

AI_ECONOMY_LABOR.label: Jobs, labour and economic transformation
AI_ECONOMY_LABOR.definition: Effects of AI on employment, work, productivity, wages and the economy, including job displacement and workforce transition.
AI_ECONOMY_LABOR.inclusion: Passages on AI replacing or transforming jobs, making people economically unnecessary, raising productivity or reshaping economies.
AI_ECONOMY_LABOR.exclusion: Wealth or power concentration among firms/states (AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION); national investment showcases (AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY).
AI_ECONOMY_LABOR.boundary_cases: Skills training responding to job disruption takes this code and AI_YOUTH_EDUCATION or AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING as applicable.

AI_YOUTH_EDUCATION.label: Youth, education and skills
AI_YOUTH_EDUCATION.definition: AI in relation to young people, schools and education: preparing youth for AI, AI literacy, AI in teaching, and disruptions such as plagiarism.
AI_YOUTH_EDUCATION.inclusion: Passages about equipping youth with AI skills, AI's effect on learning or schools, or generative AI disrupting education.
AI_YOUTH_EDUCATION.exclusion: Child online safety and exploitation (AI_CHILD_PROTECTION); international capacity-building programmes (AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING).
AI_YOUTH_EDUCATION.boundary_cases: Youth employment effects of AI can take this code and AI_ECONOMY_LABOR.

AI_CHILD_PROTECTION.label: Protecting children from AI harms
AI_CHILD_PROTECTION.definition: Risks AI poses to children: online exploitation, harmful content, manipulation, mental health, and calls to protect children in the digital space.
AI_CHILD_PROTECTION.inclusion: Passages specifically about children's safety or wellbeing in relation to AI or AI-enabled platforms.
AI_CHILD_PROTECTION.exclusion: Education and skills (AI_YOUTH_EDUCATION); general rights language (AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS).
AI_CHILD_PROTECTION.boundary_cases: National child online protection laws mentioned alongside AI also take AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY.

AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY.label: National AI strategy and achievements
AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY.definition: A speaker's own country's AI strategies, investments, programmes, regulation, pilots, institutions, talent and leadership claims, including domestic regulatory approaches such as sandboxes.
AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY.inclusion: Passages describing national AI plans, investments, data centres, public-service pilots, national AI laws or sandboxes, or claims of national AI leadership or hosting AI events and centres.
AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY.exclusion: International cooperation offered to others (AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING); calls for international rules (AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE).
AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY.boundary_cases: Hosting a UN/UNESCO AI centre takes this code and AI_UN_ROLE.

AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION.label: Power concentration, dependence and sovereignty
AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION.definition: Concern that AI power, data, compute and wealth are concentrated in a few companies or countries, creating dependence, domination or new hierarchies, and claims to digital sovereignty, national AI models or public rather than oligarchic control.
AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION.inclusion: Passages about big tech or tech oligarchs, monopolies, distrust of corporate self-regulation, technological dependence, AI as a tool of domination or neo-colonialism, and sovereign AI capacity.
AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION.exclusion: Access gaps without a power/control claim (AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE); strategic competition between great powers (AI_GEOPOLITICAL_RIVALRY); rule-making exclusion (AI_INCLUSIVE_GOVERNANCE).
AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION.boundary_cases: Anti-capitalist framing of AI as a systemic threat is coded here when it centres on concentrated control or wealth.

AI_GEOPOLITICAL_RIVALRY.label: Geopolitical competition and AI race
AI_GEOPOLITICAL_RIVALRY.definition: AI as an arena of strategic competition between powers: the AI race, technological leadership, great-power rivalry, supply-chain conflict over chips, and AI as strategic infrastructure shaping world order.
AI_GEOPOLITICAL_RIVALRY.inclusion: Passages framing AI as a race to win or lead, a driver of rivalry, fragmentation or a new arms race, or dependent on contested chip supply chains.
AI_GEOPOLITICAL_RIVALRY.exclusion: Concentration in companies or domination claims (AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION); military uses (AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS).
AI_GEOPOLITICAL_RIVALRY.boundary_cases: A call for rules rather than a race takes this code and AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

AI_OPPORTUNITY_RISK_DUALITY.label: AI as both promise and peril
AI_OPPORTUNITY_RISK_DUALITY.definition: Explicit framing of AI as double-edged: great opportunity alongside serious risk, a neutral tool whose effects depend on use, or public fears to be answered with reassurance.
AI_OPPORTUNITY_RISK_DUALITY.inclusion: Passages that pair AI's benefits with its dangers, call it a double-edged sword, or state that its impact depends on human choices.
AI_OPPORTUNITY_RISK_DUALITY.exclusion: Passages that discuss only a specific risk or only a benefit (use the specific code).
AI_OPPORTUNITY_RISK_DUALITY.boundary_cases: Duality language that leads directly into a governance call takes both this code and AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

AI_TRANSFORMATIVE_ERA.label: AI as epochal transformation
AI_TRANSFORMATIVE_ERA.definition: AI described as a defining, epochal transformation of the era or of society, often within the broader digital/ICT revolution, including reflections on the nature of intelligence or on AI and human values.
AI_TRANSFORMATIVE_ERA.inclusion: Passages calling AI a revolution comparable to steam or electricity, the defining test of the age, a force transforming how people live, or philosophical reflection on AI.
AI_TRANSFORMATIVE_ERA.exclusion: Brief listing among technologies (AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION); specific economic effects (AI_ECONOMY_LABOR).
AI_TRANSFORMATIVE_ERA.boundary_cases: Pandemic-accelerated digitalisation that names AI is coded here when AI's transformative role is described rather than just listed.

AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION.label: AI listed among technologies
AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION.definition: AI named only briefly in a neutral or positive list of technologies, trends or national strengths, without further discussion of AI itself.
AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION.inclusion: Passages where 'artificial intelligence' appears alongside other technologies (robotics, big data, quantum, biotech) with no AI-specific claim.
AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION.exclusion: AI listed among threats or crises (AI_THREAT_LIST_MENTION); any passage with an AI-specific claim (use the substantive code).
AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION.boundary_cases: A list plus one AI-specific sentence should receive the substantive code instead of, or in addition to, this code.

AI_THREAT_LIST_MENTION.label: AI listed among threats or crises
AI_THREAT_LIST_MENTION.definition: AI named briefly within a catalogue of global challenges, threats or citizen worries (conflict, climate, pandemics, disinformation, cost of living) without elaboration of the AI risk itself.
AI_THREAT_LIST_MENTION.inclusion: Passages where AI or 'unregulated AI' is one item in a list of crises, dangers or public concerns, or noted as neglected on a crowded agenda.
AI_THREAT_LIST_MENTION.exclusion: Passages that explain how AI causes the harm (use the specific risk code); neutral technology lists (AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION).
AI_THREAT_LIST_MENTION.boundary_cases: If the passage says AI is a threat and names a mechanism (e.g. weapons, disinformation), use that mechanism's code.

passages.text: For effective United Nations, it is necessary for the Security Council to be reformed to be more inclusive, accountable and responsible for maintaining international peace and security. The General Assembly must evolve into a representative policy-making body, rather than a debate club. The implementation of International Court of Justice judgments must become mandatory for all Member States, ensuring the rule of international law. Reform is needed not only for old challenges, but also for new ones. Artificial intelligence brings enormous opportunities, but also incalculable risks for our civilization. It is not just a technological leap. Its impact may be greater than the industrial and digital revolutions. Aware of this, my country and I support the proposal to make artificial intelligence a priority of the 80th session. Next year, we will elect a new Secretary-General of the United Nations. We need a person with leadership skills, with rich diplomatic experience, and ability to bring differences and build consensus, but also deeply humane and committed to the vulnerable. The next top diplomat of the world must possess knowledge, patience and tact. After 80 years, it is high time for a woman to be a Secretary-General of the United Nations. In a world dominated by strong men, often with weapons, we need strong women with wisdom and empathy. I believe that women, who along with their children are the greatest and most numerous victims of wars, have an inalienable right and obligation to prevent them. The anarchic international order is a threat to all, but especially to small states. It is natural for small and medium-sized states to be the greatest supporters of the United Nations reforms. Distinguished excellencies, let me share with you what we are doing in this regard. We supported the adoption of the Pact for the Future as a new global social contract. Living in one of the most climate vulnerable regions in the world, the Mediterranean, Macedonian citizens are already experiencing the consequences of the climate crisis, such as extreme weather conditions. That is why we supported the implementation of the Paris Agreement at COP26. 29 in Baku.

Yet, what is the point of being a privileged member state of a dysfunctional, irrelevant, marginalized international organization?

passages.text: The process to find a worthy successor to Secretary General Guterres must be a step change in the way that we work. The selection process must be transparent, inclusive, and based on merit, not political bargaining. The decision must be taken out of the corridors of this building and become a truly global conversation involving all member states, as well as civil society. As for the Security Council, Its makeup reflects the world as it was in 1945 and not as it is in 2025. Malta begs the clamour for expansion and fairer regional representation. But it isn't just the composition that needs to change. The role of the Security Council needs to be elevated. It must serve as a greater counterbalance to the dominance of the larger powers. It must also be a genuine platform for all the nations of the world to have our voices heard. And change needs to come not just to political structures, but to the way the United Nations works. All around the world, including in Malta, my country, citizens are rightly pressing governments to do more with less, better value for money. The United Nations, like any other publicly funded organization, needs to make sure that it ruthlessly focuses not on protecting the way things are done now, but on the way things can be done differently to deliver better outcomes for the same investment. No area of the United Nations can remain untouched, no vested interest left untackled. The United Nations must embrace digital diplomacy for the artificial intelligence age. Every system must be streamlined, every process scrutinized to ensure it delivers for the frontline. Every program assessed against its actual impact. We shouldn't be afraid to ensure that the United Nations stops doing things it does badly and starts doing those things it does well even better and even more efficiently. Too often, global relations, like much of life, can seem merely a numbers game. Of course, the biggest states will always have the loudest voices, and that is understandable.

I want to take this occasion to pay tribute to the Secretary-General and his unwavering commitment and dedication to the cause of peace. Thank you, Antonio. But no one can say that the big power horse trading that has marked every single election of a Secretary-General has been an edifying sight. We often reach the right outcome, and that is good and positive, but we certainly go the wrong way about it. We need to do better.
